analysis.title: weekend prep ... (Brian Garrett, Sales & Trading)
key_insights: Goldman's desk describes the market as lacking conviction: the themes and factors that carried conviction earlier in the year are being challenged, and investors are reluctant to press a directional view into year end.

2026 is described as a year with two halves. H1 had large returns (Korea +130%, SMH +80%, momentum pair +70%, AI winners +50%) and the NDX 2-month Sharpe ratio hit its highest since the late 1990s in June. H2 has been frustrating, with themes shifting from 6-month horizons to 6 days or 6 hours.

The desk's closing point: the cash market has little conviction, but the vol market is strongly convinced that November 5 was an isolated event. The SPX year-end straddle now costs less than the index moved in a single session last Thursday.
Prime brokerage data: hedge funds have sold US equities in 5 of the last 6 weeks, with long selling outpacing short covering 2.8 to 1. Net exposure is in the 2nd percentile on a 5-year lookback.
Globally, single stocks have been sold for 9 consecutive weeks (since mid-September) while macro product has been bought for 4 consecutive weeks. Funds are selling longs and covering macro shorts.

Technology was the most net sold sector this week. The US info tech long/short ratio closed the week at the lowest level on record (data from 2016), and exposure to the largest SPX sector is at its lowest in a decade.

OneDelta flow: long-only and hedge fund clients were both moderate net sellers. Long-only clients sold NVDA heavily and rotated the dollars into hyperscalers and other megacap tech, so the shift was within megacap tech and not out of it.

Futures desk: last Thursday's extreme move surprise ratio set off unwinds in vol control and risk parity. GS models show about $27bn of SPX supply from vol control over the next few sessions. These funds re-risk if vol keeps falling.

Energy: Brent fell about 20% in 7 sessions at the start of November, the sharpest drawdown outside Covid. Thursday's price and open interest action suggest new longs are entering through both futures and calls.
Index calls: indices have closed much of the gap from last Thursday's sell-off, with almost no upside call chasing. Outright long calls are a not-crowded trade.
Skew: index put/call skew has firmed. A 3-month 10% OTM put funds the 3-month ~5.5% OTM call (zero-cost risk reversal), or funds 2x 3-month 108/118 call spreads.
VIX puts have traded more volume over the last 10 sessions than at any other point this year. A VIX Dec 18/16 1x2 put spread costs about 0.50 (UX2 reference 19.4).
Implied-minus-realized vol is at its widest negative gap in over a year, and is negative for every US sector except utilities, so options markets are treating the spike as an isolated event.
SPX year-end straddle costs 4.2% versus last Thursday's -4.4% move. The NDX year-end straddle costs 6.8% versus -6.4% last Thursday.

Baskets: 12-month momentum (GSPRHIMO) has had its best outperformance versus 3-month momentum (GSPRHMO3) in GS records. AI names in the short leg of 3-month momentum have increased significantly, momentum positioning has collapsed, and consensus winners are no longer crowded.
Wall Street vs Main Street: US long/short net exposure (institutional) is diverging from AAII retail equity exposure, with retail participation undeterred (AAII data through Oct 31).

GS 2027 outlooks: Hatzius forecasts 2.8% global growth in 2027 on lower energy prices and strong capex. Wilson lists 10 market themes including a maturing cycle and an AI impulse peaking. Oppenheimer is overweight US and Japan and underweight Europe. Triveda sees the dollar firming near term and softening over 2027. Struyven recommends a positive commodities allocation despite near-zero base-case BCOM returns after 26% YTD. Rindels sees AI hardware and IP spend above $900bn by end-2026 and $1.4tn by end-2027, about 4% of US GDP.

sector_views.rationale: Hedge funds were most net sellers of tech this week and the US info tech long/short ratio is at a record low. This describes positioning, not a GS rating.
New longs are entering Brent via futures and calls after a roughly 20% drop in 7 sessions.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Hatzius expects growth on lower energy prices and strong capex. Downside risks are Iran escalation, fiscal deficits and weaker AI spending.
Struyven sees near-zero base-case returns from here but recommends a commodities allocation as a hedge.
The sharpest drawdown outside Covid. New longs are now entering.
Rindels puts 2027 spend at about 4% of US GDP.

tension_points.theme: vol market vs cash market conviction
tension_points.bull_case: Options price November 5 as an isolated event. Implied-realized spread is negative in every US sector but utilities, SPX and NDX year-end straddles cost about as much as one session's move, and calls are uncrowded. Momentum positioning has collapsed and consensus winners are no longer crowded.
tension_points.bear_case: Cash market conviction is low. Hedge fund net exposure is in the 2nd percentile, tech long/short is at a record low, and vol control and risk parity are unwinding about $27bn of SPX. Put skew has firmed on demand for downside protection.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Vol continuing to collapse would trigger vol-control and risk-parity re-risking, which the desk says will eventually happen.
